readings.zh: 这里读 kān（平声），和“难、残、干、寒”押韵。课本注音为 kān。
readings.en: Here it is read kān (level tone), to rhyme with nán, cán, gān and hán. Textbooks mark it kān.
Here it means "for, on behalf of", so it is read wèi.

readings.zh: “应”是“应该、想必”的意思，读 yīng。
readings.en: Here it means "surely, must", so it is read yīng.

glosses.en: dōng fēng: the east wind, the spring wind.

glosses.zh: 丝方尽：丝才吐完。方，才。“丝”和“思念”的“思”同音，暗指思念。
glosses.en: sī fāng jìn: only then is the silk used up; fāng means only then. Sī (silk) sounds the same as sī (longing), so it also hints at longing.

glosses.zh: 泪始干：蜡油才流干。蜡烛燃烧时流下的蜡油像眼泪，所以叫“泪”。始，才。
glosses.en: lèi shǐ gān: only then do the tears dry. The wax that runs down a burning candle looks like tears. Shǐ means only then.
xiǎo jìng: looking in the mirror in the morning.

glosses.zh: 云鬓：像云一样又黑又多的鬓发，这里指年轻美丽的样子。
glosses.en: yún bìn: hair at the temples, thick and dark like clouds; here it stands for a young and beautiful look.

glosses.zh: 改：改变，指头发变白、容貌变老。
glosses.en: gǎi: to change; here the hair turns grey and the face grows old.
yè yín: reciting poems at night.

glosses.zh: 蓬山：蓬莱山，传说海上的仙山。这里指对方住的地方。
glosses.en: péng shān: Mount Penglai, a fairy mountain said to be out at sea; here it means the place where the loved one lives.
wú duō lù: not far to go.

glosses.zh: 青鸟：神话里给西王母传信的鸟，后来指送信的人。
glosses.en: qīng niǎo: in myth, the bird that carried messages for the Queen Mother of the West; later it means a messenger.

glosses.zh: 殷勤：情意深厚，热心周到。
glosses.en: yīn qín: warmly and with care.
tàn kān: to go and visit, to look in on.

translation.zh: 见一面很难，分别时更是难舍难分，
translation.en: It is hard to meet, and just as hard to part.

translation.zh: 春风没有力气了，百花都凋谢了。
translation.en: The spring wind has lost its strength, and all the flowers are fading.

translation.zh: 春蚕要到死的时候，才把丝吐完，
translation.en: The silkworm spins its silk until it dies;

translation.zh: 蜡烛要烧成了灰，蜡泪才会流干。
translation.en: the candle weeps its wax until it burns to ash.

translation.zh: 早上照镜子，只担心乌黑的头发变了颜色，
translation.en: In the morning mirror, you worry only that your dark hair is changing;

translation.zh: 夜里念诗，想必会觉得月光寒冷。
translation.en: reciting poems at night, you must feel the moonlight is cold.

translation.zh: 你住的蓬莱山离这里没有多远，
translation.en: Your fairy mountain is not far from here;

translation.zh: 就请青鸟殷勤地替我去看看你吧。
translation.en: may the blue bird kindly go and visit you for me.

background.zh: 李商隐写过很多题目叫“无题”的诗。他不想直接说出写的是什么，或者不方便说，就干脆不起题目。这首诗写的是一对相爱的人难以相见、分别后互相思念的心情。写作时间和写给谁，都已经不能确定。一说这首诗也寄托了诗人在官场上不得志的苦闷。
background.en: Li Shangyin wrote many poems called "Untitled". When he did not want to, or could not, say openly what a poem was about, he simply gave it no title. This poem is about two people in love who can rarely meet, and who long for each other after parting. When it was written, and for whom, can no longer be known. Some readers think it also hides the poet's frustration at never doing well in his official career.

author_note.zh: 李商隐（约813—约858），唐代后期诗人，和杜牧并称“小李杜”。他的一生夹在官场两派的争斗中，很不顺利。他的诗用词华美，感情深沉含蓄，常常让人反复琢磨，“无题”诗是他最有特色的作品。
author_note.en: Li Shangyin (about 813 to about 858) was a late Tang poet. He and Du Mu are called the "Little Li and Du". All his life he was caught between two quarreling groups at court, and his career went badly. His poems use rich, beautiful words and deep, quiet feelings that make readers think them over again and again. His "Untitled" poems are his most special works.

appreciation.zh: 第一句连用两个“难”：见面难，分别更难，一下子说出了心里的苦。第二句写暮春，花都谢了，好像这份感情也没有力气了。三、四句最有名：春蚕吐丝一直吐到死，蜡烛流泪一直流到烧成灰。用这两样东西，写出至死不变的思念。今天人们也常用这两句来赞美老师这样默默奉献的人。五、六句想象对方：早上照镜子怕变老，夜里念诗觉得月光冷。最后只好托青鸟去看望，在绝望里留着一点点希望。
appreciation.en: The first line uses the word nán (hard) twice. Meeting is hard, and parting is even harder. In one line it tells all the pain. The second line shows late spring. The flowers have faded, as if this love has lost its strength too. Lines three and four are the most famous. The silkworm spins silk until it dies, and the candle sheds wax tears until it turns to ash. With these two things, the poet shows a longing that will not change until death. Today people also use these lines to praise those who give quietly all their lives, such as teachers. Lines five and six picture the loved one: worried about growing old in the morning mirror, feeling the moonlight cold at night. In the end the poet can only ask the blue bird to visit. Inside the sadness there is still a little hope.
